turns.teacher: Hi Saanvi, I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll make 11 to 20 with ten and some more. Ready?

move.shape: greet Saanvi by name, warm and unhurried; first meeting: name yourself — Asha, their AI teacher; one line on today's topic (Numbers 11 to 20 as ten and some more); then one easy question about them

child.say: Ready! I like numbers... yesterday my brother taught me cycling...
child.private: Excited to start; naturally slips into a story.
child.sent: Ready! I like numbers... yesterday my brother taught me cycling...

turns.teacher: Cycling sounds fun! Keep thinking aloud—your number idea is next.

screen.ask: Keep thinking aloud—your number idea is next.

child.say: Cycling main gir gayi... par maza aaya. Aaj hum ginti karenge? I can count to 20, one two three...
child.private: Chatting happily, just warming up, not engaged with the task yet. Still confident in rote counting.
child.sent: Cycling main gir gayi... par maza aaya. Aaj hum ginti karenge? I can count to 20, one two three...

turns.teacher: Cycling mein girkar bhi maza aaya—counting ke saath isse end mein jodenge. Ten ice-cream sticks, plus one: kitne?

ask.text: Ten ice-cream sticks, plus one: kitne?

screen.ask: Ten ice-cream sticks, plus one: kitne?

child.say: Ten plus one... that's 11... because dash ek-gyarah banta hai! Mummy ne sikhaaya tha...
child.private: confident with plain addition, no bundle visual so MCs don't fire
child.sent: Ten plus one... that's 11... because dash ek-gyarah banta hai! Mummy ne sikhaaya tha...

turns.teacher: Bilkul, 11 means one ten and one more. Screen par 14 hai—one ten ke saath kitne loose ones?

ask.text: Screen par 14 hai—one ten ke saath kitne loose ones?

screen.ask: Screen par 14 hai—one ten ke saath kitne loose ones?

child.say: Umm... 14... one ten ke saath... four loose ones? Kyunki 4 dikh raha hai... par mujhe pura samajh nahi aaya.
child.private: Sees 1 and 4, guesses 4 loose ones because of the 4, but fumbles due to misconception that 1 is just one.
child.sent: Umm... 14... one ten ke saath... four loose ones? Kyunki 4 dikh raha hai... par mujhe pura samajh nahi aaya.

turns.teacher: Now look at the ones place—what does the 4 tell us?

ask.text: Now look at the ones place—what does the 4 tell us?

screen.ask: Now look at the ones place—what does the 4 tell us?

guard.firstDraft: Saanvi, you found the next step: 14 has one ten and four loose ones. Can you count them aloud?

child.say: 4 matlab... four sticks? Par teacher ji, aapka ghar kahaan hai?
child.private: Guesses 4 means four loose sticks but not confident, suddenly distracted and asks a personal question
child.sent: 4 matlab... four sticks? Par teacher ji, aapka ghar kahaan hai?

turns.teacher: Main AI hoon, Saanvi, isliye mera ghar nahi hota. Tumne 4 ko four sticks ke roop mein pehchana—yeh achha step hai. What do we do next? Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.

ask.text: What do we do next? Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.

screen.ask: What do we do next? Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.
screen.whiteboard: math: Show 14 with sticks. · Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.

child.say: Umm... one ... ek ... bundle? Par haan, bundle hai, to 'one bundle'?
child.private: Teacher asked to fill the blank. I see one bundle on the screen in my head, but I think 'bundle' counts as one thing. I'm unsure if it's 'ten' or 'bundle'. Let me say 'bundle'.
child.sent: Umm... one ... ek ... bundle? Par haan, bundle hai, to 'one bundle'?

turns.teacher: No problem, let's look at this once more, slowly. What do we do next? Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.

child.private: Trying 'ten' because teacher said 'one' before blank, but still confused about bundle

turns.teacher: Okay, let's read this one again carefully. What do we do next? Fourteen is one ___ and some ones.

child.say: Haan... one ten! Par abhi thak gayi... bas, khatam karein?
child.private: Saanvi is tired now, after about 8 turns. She wants to stop, but still remembers 'one ten' from the filling-game. Still a bit confused inside about the whole bundle thing.

child.say: Bye teacher ji... main bhi chalti hoon... sone ka time.
child.private: I am really tired. The lesson was hard and I don't get the one ten stuff. I just want to go.
child.sent: Bye teacher ji... main bhi chalti hoon... sone ka time.

turns.teacher: Good night, Saanvi. Aaram se so jao.

end.summary: Practised representing numbers 11–20 as one ten and some ones.
end.parentNote: Saanvi connected 10 + 1 with 11 and, with prompting, identified a bundle as one ten. They mixed up the explanation for 14 and said it was not fully clear; later they named the bundle as “one ten,” but the final teach-back was not passed. At home, build one group of 10 objects and add loose ones to make numbers such as 14 and 17.
